Charles Fuggitt King (born January 6, 1998) is an American professional baseball pitcher. He was signed by the Philadelphia Phillies in January 2024 and is currently playing for the Double A Reading Fighting Phils.
Amateur Career
Charles King was born on January 6, 1998, and attended Coppell High School in Texas.  As a junior, he was selected to both the Under Armor All American and Perfect Game rosters in 2015.  He chose to play in the Perfect Game Series as they were both scheduled on the same weekend.  The Coppell Cowboys went into the 2016 season ranked 3rd in the country led by King.  He threw a complete game/no hitter in the 2016 playoffs vs McKinney Boyd.  He was subsequently ranked the 2nd overall RHP in Texas/ 9th countrywide, with a fast ball up to 95 and PG rating of 10/10 as ranked by Perfect Game Scouts.
Texas Christian University - TCU
King was slated to be taken early in the 2016 draft but, through his advisor, notified teams that he would instead be attending college and waived the process.  He committed to Texas Christian University. King picked up his first career win in Omaha at the College World series with 3 1/3 shutout innings against Florida June 23, 2023, where he fanned five in the game and allowed just one hit while being named player of the game. Florida went on to win the CWS.  In the summer of 2017 King played in the New England Collegiate League for the Newport Gulls where he tallied a 2.57 ERA.  King finalized his college career leading as a team captain and logging over 254 innings with a 3.93 ERA.  He served in several key roles including Saturday night starter and long reliever and pitched several complete games.
Knowing that he has some mechanical issues he wanted to address, King waived the draft again in 2021 and instead chose to intern with Zach Dechant, strength and Conditioning expert and Assistant Athletic Coach at TCU.  He then spent two seasons as a sports science and performance analyst with the MiLB division of the San Diego Padres working with both the Double A Missions in San Antonio and Single A Storm in Lake Elsinore California.
During the offseason, King trained with Driveline to analyze and refine his own mechanics. Those changes resulted in increased velocity (up to 98 mph) and significant improvement in pitch location and off-speed pitches.     This led to King being signed to a minor league contract with the Philadelphia Phillies in January 2024.
Professional Career
Jersey Shore Blue Claws - Philadelphia Phillies High A
King spent 2024 pitching in relief for the Jersey Shore Blue Claws. He made his professional debut April 6, 2024. earning a five out save to top Aberdeen 7–6. He went on to appear in 31 games and pitched 38 innings. He had a 2W-2L record with 41 strikeouts and a 4.26 ERA. In late 2024 he made a brief appearance with Reading (1.1 IP) after being promoted from Jersey Shore.
Reading Fighting Phils - Philadelphia Phillies Double A
In 2025 he transitioned into a starter role as one of the Fightin Phils' more consistent arms. He appeared in 25 games with 23 starts. tallying a record of 8W - 6L with an ERA of 4.38. He pitched 123 innings with 105 strikeouts.  He was named the "Broadway Charlie Wagner Unsung Hero" at the close of the season.   King was a steady piece of the Fightin Phils rotation all season long and was amongst the team leaders in wins, starts, innings pitched and strikeouts.
